text:
### Observed differences

- Before, the six activities A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 each ran exactly once in every trace (participation 100 in 100). In the later window, A28, A30 and A31 each appear in about 47 in 100 traces, and A32, A33 and A34 in about 56 in 100, still at most once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- The six activities split into two groups that became alternatives. Before, every pair among them co-occurred in 100 in 100 traces, with the A28/A30/A31 group always running before the A32/A33/A34 group. In the later window, A28, A30 and A31 still appear together or not at all (together in about 47 in 100 traces, both absent in the rest), A32, A33 and A34 likewise (together in about 56 in 100), while a pair from different groups co-occurs in only about 2 in 100 traces. [REL013, REL014, REL018, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL015, REL019, REL022]
- A25 and A26 still occur in every trace in both windows. Before, A25 always preceded all six activities and all six always preceded A26. In the later window, A25 precedes whichever group runs and A26 follows it: each of them appears with the A28/A30/A31 group in about 47 in 100 traces and with the A32/A33/A34 group in about 56 in 100. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, POS001, POS002]
- Transitions changed accordingly. Before, A25's observed outgoing transitions went only to A28, A30 and A31 (about 34%, 37% and 30%); in the later window they spread over all six activities (roughly 14–20% each). Direct transitions from A28, A30 and A31 to A26 appeared (about 34%, 35% and 26% of those activities' observed outgoing transitions), while their transitions into A32, A33 and A34 fell from roughly 9–14% to about 1%. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Where a group is skipped, event distances shrink: the gap from A25 to A32, A33 or A34 was 4–5 events before and is 1–3 events in about 97 in 100 later observations; the gap from A28, A30 or A31 to A26 likewise fell from 4–5 events to 1–3 events. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG008, LAG011]
- Positions shifted only slightly, in the direction shorter traces would produce: the median position of A32–A34 moved from about 0.78 to 0.75 of the trace and of A28–A31 from about 0.69 to 0.75; A25 moved slightly later (about 0.63 to 0.68) and A26 slightly earlier (about 0.85 to 0.82). These are position shifts and do not by themselves show relocation. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A25 and A26 changed from a fixed sequence that always ran both sub-blocks — first A28, A30 and A31, then A32, A33 and A34 — into a choice between the two: in the later window, about 47 in 100 cases run A28–A30–A31 and continue directly to A26, about 56 in 100 run A32–A33–A34 directly after A25, and both sub-blocks appear together in only about 2 in 100 cases. The signs are direct and consistent: participation fell exactly along the two group boundaries while co-occurrence within each group was preserved; cross-group co-occurrence collapsed from 100 to about 2 in 100 traces; new direct transitions A28/A30/A31 → A26 and A25 → A32/A33/A34 appeared; and event distances shrank from 4–5 to 1–3 exactly where a sub-block is bypassed. Every item's difference also exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and the volume of evidence far exceeds what chance produces: 58 items qualified where roughly 0.63 would be expected without a change (control-flow family, 127 units tested). Limitations: the evidence covers only this segment, so it cannot show what determines which sub-block a case takes, and it cannot rule out that the split reflects a change in the case mix entering the segment rather than in the routing between A25 and A26 itself; the small cross-group overlap could also be a rare both-sub-blocks path or sampling noise. Independent skipping of the six activities is effectively ruled out, because different-group pairs would then co-occur far more often than about 2 in 100. [OCC001, OCC004, REL013, REL015, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG004]

Other differences: only minor positional side-effects fall outside the main hypothesis — A25 sits slightly later and A26 slightly earlier in the trace with somewhat wider spread, consistent with the shorter traces left after one sub-block is skipped — and the internal order within each group of three remained unfixed, with both orders in similar proportions, in both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL013, REL025]
